paper.arxiv.2511.10507

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2511.10507v2. Rubric-based benchmark/training and differing reward-design conditions establish annotation/evaluation protocol scope. Partial rubric scores remain distinct from all-or-nothing pass rates. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Rubric verifiers can be reward-hacked and can misjudge individual criteria; the authors leave a comprehensive reward-design study to future work, while their ablation compares all-or-nothing, fractional and hybrid rewards on one base model.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AdvancedIF retains prompts that trigger final-turn instruction-following failures; the same human annotator writes the prompt and decomposed rubric, and evaluation requires every applicable final-turn criterion to pass.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

AdvancedIF contains 1, 645 dialogs across complex instructions, carried context and system steerability; RIFL separately uses human rubric/verification data to train a rubric generator and a verifier through supervised and reinforcement learning stages.
